declaredNegativeControls.law: The family list narrows the control list by being more specific about one family root. It never replaces it, so the effective set is the union and a silent family inherits the full control list.

ingressEquivalence.meaning: Both ingress doors produced the same painted result on the same DOM. Static/DB equivalence is a measured diff here, not an inference from two separate runs.

resolved.meaning: Rhythm scales the room around a control, never the control. Bound to control-bearing targets deliberately: a LAYOUT container's intrinsic height legitimately grows when its gaps grow, so checking this everywhere would report the intended effect as a violation. Includes the indirect vectors a rule could use to change the control's rendered size without touching height/block-size directly: max-height (the physical dual of max-block-size), aspect-ratio (a fixed width plus a moved aspect-ratio moves height too), scale, zoom and contain-intrinsic-size. The two `@rect-*` reserved observables are the RENDERED box read from getBoundingClientRect, so a padding/border/transform mutation that changes what is actually painted cannot hide behind an unmoved computed longhand.
Rhythm is a spacing axis. It shares no channel with the type scale, so no measured element may change a font metric under it.
Rhythm shares no channel with any palette seed.
Border geometry belongs to the shape axis. Radius is included on purpose: a rhythm stop that moved a corner would be reaching a channel it does not own.

provenance.stylesheetLaw: A static arm removes by re-serving the baseline BYTES, so removal and baseline must hash identically and the mutation must not. A DB arm never changes the sheet, so all three hashes agree and its restore law lives in the inline memo instead.

question: Does this control CAUSE the intended change, leave the declared negative controls untouched, and restore the baseline exactly when removed - through both tenant ingress doors on one scene?

scopeOfRun.note: A fixture that names a real component takes its element shape FROM THAT COMPONENT — rendered, then pasted — never from the CSS. Deriving the shape from the CSS is what let `button-modern-md` and `input-modern-md` sit on `.ds-btn`/`.ds-input` for months: a selector states what an element must carry to be MATCHED, and says nothing about whether any component emits it, so a CSS-derived fixture can measure a rule that never paints and still look green. Regenerate a component shape by rendering the engine implementation with `renderToStaticMarkup` and pasting the result, minus React-generated ids, plus `data-probe`. The synthetic fixtures (the two skeleton controls and the token readout) are exempt: they exist to read a dial, not to stand for a component. `requiresSelectors` is not documentation either: the harness asserts each string occurs verbatim in the CSS it is about to measure and marks the fixture `unmatched` if it does not, so a fixture that stops being matched is reported, never silently measured as zero. Pin selectors and the paint statement, never a declaration's VALUE — a precedence ruling would then read as a broken fixture.

controlLiveness.meaning: Every arm demonstrated a live control: each arm's own direct-dial fixture moved, checked independently rather than inferred from one arm to the other.

db-tenant-theme.meaning: At least one control moved under the dial, so the harness demonstrably observes movement. Inert verdicts in this artifact are about the CSS, not the instrument.
